section: 3. Express Ticket Purchase and the Smith Mansion Fire
description: Rush to Victoria Station to buy tickets, visit Professor Smith at night only to find the mansion engulfed in flames, a mysterious figure emerges from the fire carrying an unconscious injured person and disappears into the night

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "When are you all planning to go back?"

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Tomorrow? Feels like things here are pretty much wrapped up."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Barring any surprises, it should be tomorrow."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Then before we leave, let's visit Professor Smith again and treat him to a meal."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Speaking of which, should we visit Professor Smith once more before leaving? To say goodbye."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "There's no harm in that."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Then let's go, be uninvited guests one more time."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Go to Smith's house

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Prepare to go to Smith's house to confirm the order

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: At nine in the evening, as you drive towards the direction of the Smith residence, you notice a bright light in the distant, silent darkness... a deep black plume of smoke rising straight into the sky from the light.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Hmm, it's on fire."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "As expected, something unexpected happened."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: When you enter the street of the Smith residence, you realize it's not lights or fireworks, but a house fiercely ablaze, and that house is the one you raided last night!

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: oh guys, its so hot now

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Let's go, we should check out the situation."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Try to crack a joke to lighten the mood

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "It's as hot as a house on fire."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "I hope Professor Smith doesn't turn into Professor Scorch."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "I'll call the police first."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: In the distant firelight, you see a figure carrying someone slowly walking out of the flames.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Take out phone to call the police

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: #See if this figure looks familiar.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: player4's mind somehow combines mobile and phone into a single word.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Give up on the idea of calling the police

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Look at the figure, and also scan the surroundings for nearby pedestrians.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: You approach and find the figure is James Beddoes, who is panting heavily while carrying Professor Smith.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Oh my god."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Professor Smith's clothes are almost completely burned off, and his skin has extensive injuries.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Take over Professor Smith to check his condition.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Search for nearby pedestrians.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Don't worry, I'm a doctor. Please let me check the situation."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Beddoes discovers you and anxiously asks for help, "Thank heavens, save us."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "What caused the fire for you two?" #While helping the two, preparing to take them away from this dangerous place.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Many passersby gather around, some watching, some trying to put out the fire with buckets, some screaming loudly. The firefighters should arrive soon.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: .ra First Aid

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: Belief arises from desire; if it is what you hope for, it will be answered. <player4>'s First Aid prayer: D100=75/70 Failure - Well... just missed by a bit.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Professor Smith's burns are very severe. player4 tries to remove the tattered clothing from his body, but the clothes have stuck to his wounds. The fabric player4 removes tears Smith's wounds a second time.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: .ra First Aid

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: Belief arises from desire; if it is what you hope for, it will be answered. <player4>'s First Aid prayer: D100=22/70 Hard Success - That should be able to compete with others' successes, right...?

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Calm down, calm down, think about what you learned in school. #Clenching teeth and carefully treating the wound.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: player4 stops in time to avoid further injury, takes out first aid tools from the backpack, and simply treats the wound. Beddoes quickly thanks you. Then he says, "Please help take us to 2 Cheapside Street."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Hmm, where is this?" "Sir, both of you are seriously injured and need to go to the hospital."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Thank you very much. The professor was framed by a group of people who have a grudge against him."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Forget it, let's go first..."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "So we can't go to the hospital; it's a public place." "Those damned criminals will harm the professor again."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Let's go. I can treat your wounds."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "We need to go somewhere they don't know."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "On the way, let the doctor treat the wounds simply first, and also tell us what exactly happened, so we can better protect the professor."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: [First Aid]

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "No time to lose." #Helping Beddoes carry the professor into the car.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: You get into the car and leave the place. After a while, the surrounding noise fades into the silence of the night. Only then does the professor struggle to sit up, gasping for breath to greet you, completely unlike his usual booming voice. The professor begins to speak weakly with trembling words. "Cough... I feel I can't speak for much longer... so I'll be brief..." "I have been tracking an evil artifact, the Sedefekar Simulacrum... It's a statue, a source of powerful magic..." "In the late 18th century, it was dismantled... Fragments are scattered across Europe... I intended to retrieve the fragments and destroy them..." "My speech at the Challenger Lecture event... aimed to attract people who might help him, but my enemies soon found me." "Just a short while ago, Beddoes and I were attacked at home by Turkish madmen... I believe they are also searching for the Sedefekar Simulacrum... but for evil purposes..." "The Turks tried to burn us alive... but Beddoes saved me..." "And of course, you." "My notes were burned in the fire... They might also have fallen into the hands of the Turks... In any case... the statue must absolutely not fall into their hands..." "I beg you to collect the simulacrum fragments before those assassins succeed..."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "What are the characteristics of these fragments?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "I still have some remaining assets and notes at 2 Cheapside Street... I will give them all to you there... as payment and clues..."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Will you pay?" #Rubbing hands like a fly.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: After saying these words, Professor Smith coughs, begins to gasp heavily, and can no longer speak. Your car also stops at the destination: 2 Cheapside Street. It is located in a dirty building on an ordinary street. The valet helps the professor out of the car and opens the house. The house is full of dust, indicating it is not often used.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Follow into the house.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: After helping Professor Smith into bed, the valet rummages in a cabinet and pulls out a suitcase and a small notebook.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: #Before closing the door, cautiously observe the surroundings to see if anyone else is paying attention to this place.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Fan the dust in front of the face, follow the professor into the house.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: .ra Spot Hidden

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: Belief arises from desire; if it is what you expect, it will be answered. <player5>'s Investigation Wish:

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Take a look at the room's furnishings.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Then Bailan will find that there are no other people on this street.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Take the small notebook and briefly flip through it.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Read the notebook together with player4.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "This is all the property we have left."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Shrugs shoulders. "You know, my boss doesn't really care about these things."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "But we still very much hope you can help. We have nothing left to give you; the fire burned everything we had."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "But I think she would like your plan."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "It's okay, Professor. I'm happy to help."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Thank you again for your generosity."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "I think my Lord would not want to see evil running rampant in the world either."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "You should thank my boss. If she knew a whole room of your books was burned, she'd probably be rolling around in bed."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Hmm, no problem. Leave this matter to us."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "So, should we refund the plane tickets? Hope there won't be too much handling fee."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Hope so."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Rubs forehead. "I need to tell my boss first."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Please... depart as soon as possible.."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Pick up the suitcase and hurry out to the nearest telegraph office to send a telegram to Claire and report the professor's situation.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Then you can receive a reply in about 17 hours.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Sigh, we have to set off next..."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: It is now 11 PM.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Forgot about the damn time difference. "I'll send it after I get on the train."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "I think we should sleep first and make specific arrangements tomorrow? It's already late."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "That's true, but we need to stay alert."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Let's find a place to sleep nearby first. I need to wait for the telegram anyway, though I might not get it."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Okay."

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: Prayers received! Continuing to record the horror of the Orient Express for you. Currently recorded texts: 693, time used: 3 hours 19 minutes 46 seconds.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: January 5th

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Check if the telegram has been sent back.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The telegram will arrive at 4 PM today.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Shake the other two awake, indicating it's time to go.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Should we decide where to go first?"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "We should learn about this train first."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "A route that traverses Europe, the European gentlemen love this train."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "I really don't know much about Europe..."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Hmm, and where is the starting station?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "To be honest, aside from a few business trips, I'm not much better off than you."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: So,

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Walk over and sit beside him, order a coffee. "The weather is quite nice today, isn't it, sir?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: He sizes you up, then puts down his coffee, takes off his hat, and greets you.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Quite lucky for a traveler like me." #Return the greeting. "Please excuse me for not wearing a hat."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "May I ask what brings you here, sir?" the other party inquires politely.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "It's like this, my friends and I have come from afar, wanting to see the sights of London and the renowned Orient Express. To be precise, it was initiated by another friend who couldn't make it."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "So you'd like me to recommend places worth visiting in London, is that it?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Because she was held up by local matters, and she booked the tickets." #Frown, putting on a pained expression. "So we don't know the train's departure point."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Oh, the Orient Express has many departure points. The nearest train station from here is Victoria Station, about a mile south of Buckingham Palace."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Ask the other two. "Shall we go and board here? How about Paris for the first stop?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Thank you for the directions, have a pleasant day." Drink the coffee in hand in one gulp and go to meet up with companions.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "You're welcome. It's my pleasure to give directions to a respectable gentleman."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "My respects to you again, my kind friend."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Hmm... So the nearest departure point is also quite close from here."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Shall we go?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: A newspaper boy comes up to you. "Ladies and gentlemen, would you like to buy a newspaper?"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: #Habitually take out pounds, deciding to buy a newspaper to see the situation.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Is that so? One copy, thank you."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: #Also check if there are any reports related to last night's fire.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "A man named Mohammed died three times in a row!"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Let's go, although I wanted to wait for the boss's telegram."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Shall we go, let's set off?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Then turns and walks towards the vehicle

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: #Prepares to head to the station

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "So where's our first stop?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Are you as rich as the boss, able to charter the entire train?"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "We probably can only go by train first, so wherever the train goes, we'll go there first."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Exactly."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Oh, I thought we had to buy tickets from the starting station to the terminal station."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Then

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Walks to the ticket office, indicating a need for three tickets

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: In the early morning, a queue had already formed in the ticket hall of Victoria Station. In front of the wooden ticket windows, people stamped their feet to ward off the cold. Ticket clerks pushed hard cardboard tickets through the iron grilles, their fingers slightly stained blue from ink. Half an hour later, it was finally your turn. The clerk mechanically repeated the fares and departure times, his voice carrying the distinctive weariness of a London accent.
